name: Model-specific replacement knobs for discontinued appliances
buyer: Homeowners, small landlords and property managers with a range, oven or heater whose control knob or dial is broken and no longer sold
pain: The OEM part is discontinued, generic knobs don't match, and the only exact match is a used part at a high price. Free DIY files exist but need CAD, printing and gluing.
wedge: Sell by appliance model and part number with a pre-modeled, fit-tested catalog in heat-resistant filament. The buyer does one step: order by model number. There is no CAD, photo matching or gluing.

scan1Edge.entrant_basis: The entrant pre-models knobs by appliance model and part number, so the buyer picks the model and orders. This needs a catalog-building grind using calipers and a basic printer, with no licences or network.
scan1Edge.falsifier: If Etsy or eBay sellers already list knobs by model number at or below $25 with ship times of 3 days or less, or if the catalog can't reach enough models to get repeat orders, the edge disappears.
scan1Edge.unit: buyer steps to a working knob

unitEconomicsNoted.notes: The $15-25 target price and the 60-75% material margin are the notes' own estimates. Marketplace fees, labor and shipping are not modeled, so real margin is lower.

majorUncertainty: Whether enough buyers will search by model or part number and pay $15-25, and whether the entrant can build a fit-tested catalog fast enough.
unknowns: Current eBay and new OEM prices (RepairClinic etc.) were not retrieved
Heat resistance needs (PETG, ASA or nylon) are from the notes, not from the excerpts

regulatoryOrPlatformDependency: Depends on Etsy and eBay for discovery. There is product-liability exposure on gas range controls, and care is needed with OEM part numbers and trademarks.

evidence.shows: A 2016 eBay review says the used market charged $289.95 per discontinued Thermador knob. The price is old.
evidence.quote: Until now, the used market was a monopoly and there was one source charging $289.95 per knob, sheer market arrogance.

evidence.shows: The same 2016 review says a 3D-printed replacement knob was available at $60.00. It shows the pattern, not today's price.
evidence.quote: Now, with sharpeibear there is an alternative at $60.00 per knob, a replacement built via 3D Printing.
